scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the task: app/Models/Queue.php, app/Models/Ticket.php, app/Actions/IssueTicket.php, app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php, database/factories/TicketFactory.php, the single migration, the three docs files, and the tests; no unrelated refactors, files or features.

issues.explanation: down() re-adds the old unique index (queue_id, code) while issue_date still exists, so migrate:rollback throws a duplicate-key error as soon as one queue has issued the same prefix number on two days, which is the normal case after the first day; the rollback needs to remove/deduplicate later-day tickets (documenting the loss) or skip restoring the old unique index.

The migration wraps change() in a catch-all and adds a ~35-line hand-rolled SQLite table rebuild plus a MariaDB-only raw ALTER, duplicating what Laravel's native column change already does and risking a masked real schema failure.

The map is validated in UpdateQueue before saving and again by the model's saving hook, although the action already converts the model's InvalidArgumentException, so the pre-check is redundant and the two paths can drift.

There is no test for the migration (backfill from DATE(issued_at), NOT NULL, index swap) and the UpdateQueue path only exercises the duplicate-letter case, not malformed keys/values or an unauthorized caller with the new argument.
The test name still says "continues the sequence past A999" while its assertions were changed to N codes.
nextCode() still defaults to the legacy 'A' prefix, which no production caller uses and which would resurrect the old A-series sequence if called without a prefix.

review.summary: Adds priority-derived ticket prefixes (N/P/E by default, per-queue override) and per-day numbering via tickets.issue_date, with issuance, factory, UpdateQueue validation, migration, docs and tests. The forward path is solid and well tested, but the migration's down() re-adds the old (queue_id, code) unique index and will fail on rollback once a prefix number repeats across days; the migration also carries a speculative SQLite rebuild/raw-ALTER fallback and the map is validated twice, so I would request fixes before merging.
